newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar to tender Friday for 2,500T soyoil.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar to tender Friday for 2,500T soyoil.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender on Friday for a shipment of 2,500 tonnes of soyoil, company officials said on Thursday.
The shipment would be slated for delivery by the end of May, a company official said.
Taiwan edible oil producers have been cutting their soybean imports and turning to soyoil imports as a result of the island's hog foot and mouth disease epidemic.

Since it erupted on March 20, the epidemic and subsequent mass slaughter of some two million hogs has caused a significant drop in the island's demand for soymeal feed, forcing edible oil producers to cut soybean crushing to trim soymeal inventories.
Soyoil production also has fallen as the crush rate has been reduced, forcing producers to turn to crude soyoil imports to make up for the shortfall.
Soybean crushing yields two main products, oil and soymeal. Crushing to produce oil would result in a fast-growing surplus of meal for which there is no demand, crushers explained.
